name: Ironwood Plastics Inc.
old_description: Since 1979, Ironwood Plastics has been a leader in the plastics industry. Founded by Gordon K. Stephens, the company was sold to CTB, Inc., a Berkshire Hathaway Company, in 2010.  We recognize that technology is constantly changing and our state-of-the-art facilities in Ironwood, Michigan and Two Rivers, Wisconsin enable us to stay ahead of the latest trends and technologies, giving our clients the highest quality products to meet their unique specifications.
about:
Ironwood Plastics Inc. was founded in 1979 by Gordon K. Stephens in Ironwood, Michigan. The company was acquired by CTB, Inc., a Berkshire Hathaway subsidiary, in 2010 and operates today as a division of that organization. A second production site was established in Two Rivers, Wisconsin, giving the company a dual-facility footprint in the Upper Midwest.

The company specializes in custom injection molding with a focus on complex, high-precision processes. Its core capabilities include two-shot molding, reel-to-reel molding, insert molding, close-tolerance molding, and overmolding. A scientific, data-driven approach to process development and optimization underpins production, and secondary services such as pad printing, sonic welding, and tape-and-reel packaging provide a single-source solution. The management team brings more than 200 years of combined plastics-industry experience.

Primary markets served are automotive, electronics, and medical. Automotive projects have included HVAC damper components, fuel-pressure sensors, cylinder-deactivation valves, and inlet check valves for plastic fuel tanks. Electronics work centers on reel-to-reel insert-molded connectors and sensor components requiring zero-defect quality. Medical applications are referenced in the context of tight-tolerance molding for critical devices.

Ironwood's stated vision since inception has been "to be a world class injection molder of complex projects." The company differentiates itself through its engineering-driven methodology, investment in in-line inspection and vision-assisted automation, and a partnership model that emphasizes traceability from resin receipt through finished product.
